description: OS inventory and OS-level resource limits: build/version spread, process and handle headroom, paging and virtual memory. Inventory first, pressure second.

panels.description: Hosts where this collector failed its last scrape. Non-zero means the numbers on this page are incomplete - see the Collector scrape health row at the bottom.
panels.title: Scrape FAIL

panels.description: Distinct OS versions in the selection. A high number means an inconsistent, hard-to-patch estate.
panels.title: OS Builds

panels.description: Hosts reporting OS inventory.
panels.title: Hosts

panels.description: Hosts near the OS process limit. New processes will fail to start.
panels.title: Process Headroom < 20%

panels.description: Most logged-on users on a single host.

panels.description: Lowest pagefile headroom reported by WMI.

panels.description: Busiest hosts by process count.

panels.description: Pagefile headroom, worst first.

panels.description: Primary view for this collector: what is actually installed. Filter the Version column to find hosts stuck on an old build.

panels.description: OS-level ceilings. Process Used % and Virtual Free % are the two that cause hard failures rather than slowness.

panels.description: Grow the pagefile or reduce memory demand on these hosts.
panels.title: Hotspots: Paging Free % < 20

panels.description: A staircase that never comes down is a process leak. Series capped with topk/bottomk to stay readable on a large fleet. Filter Server to see everything.

panels.description: How close each host is to the hard OS process ceiling.

panels.description: Session count over time - shows shift patterns and stuck sessions.

panels.description: Pagefile headroom over time.
panels.title: Paging Free % (bottomk 10)

panels.description: Both must stay positive. Virtual exhaustion with free physical memory means address-space fragmentation.

panels.description: Confirms the Prometheus instance label matches the real machine name and domain.
panels.title: Hostname & Domain

panels.description: Mixed timezones make log correlation painful and can break scheduled jobs.
panels.title: Timezone

panels.description: Difference between the host clock and the scrape time. See Collector time for the authoritative NTP view.
panels.title: OS Clock Skew vs Prometheus (topk 10)

panels.description: Maximum memory a single process may commit. Low values on a 64-bit host indicate a policy or WOW64 constraint.
panels.title: Process Memory Limit (bottomk 10)

panels.description: FAIL rows mean every metric on this dashboard is stale for that host. Fix the exporter first, then re-read the KPIs.
panels.title: Scrape Health by Host

panels.description: Growing duration usually means the host is under load or the collector is querying more objects. Series capped with topk/bottomk to stay readable on a large fleet. Filter Server to see everything.
panels.title: Scrape Duration (topk 10)

panels.description: Dips to 0 mark scrape gaps. Correlate with the flat spots you see in the trend panels above.
